messages.author: ca503561ceb45d04
messages.subject: (single) Instance file generation and usage - MATLAB.
parts:
Hi Team IRACE,

Is it possible if I could get  an example on how to create instances  (with one single instance file(text)) for simple function calls with different values for a particular parameter/variable (this need not be optimized).  Something similar to the benchmark instance generations.  I saw this example on the technical report but I can not seem to make it work. Perhaps I am  not using the right syntax.  I am using matlab and seems like I am stuck with this for the last few hours.  Any extra quick example (matlab based) would be appreciated.  I guess the minimal matlab example has not been sufficient (for me).  Hope to hear soon.  

Regards,
Bali

messages.author: 854a0709976c2a48
messages.subject: Re: (single) Instance file generation and usage - MATLAB.
parts:
Hi Bali,

If you mean that you have a benchmark function in your code that takes different instance parameters, you can create a trainInstancesFile (instances.txt) file like:

myfunction n=2 d=10
myfunction n=2 d=20
myfunction n=2 d=30
myfunction n=3 d=30

Then irace will pass something like "myfunction n=2 d=10" to target-runner and target-runner needs to pass that to your matlab code.

MATLAB is tricky to configure because it cannot be made executable, like other programming languages, and it is hard to pass parameters to it and run it as a stand-alone program. The example we distribute with irace used to work some time ago. It seems every new version of Matlab becomes worse at this!

If you know R, there is a matlabr package that may help. Then, you can write targetRunner as an R function that directly interfaces with matlab code.

Otherwise, you have to figure out how to pass parameters to your matlab code from target-runner in some other way. One possible approach could be to write in target-runner a file containing all the info that you need (instance, parameters values, seed) and make your matlab code read that file and set the variables. There are other ways you can find around:

https://www.mathworks.com/matlabcentral/answers/97204-how-can-i-pass-input-parameters-when-running-matlab-in-batch-mode-in-windows

https://stackoverflow.com/questions/3335505/how-can-i-pass-command-line-arguments-to-a-standalone-matlab-executable-running

But I don't know which methods work with recent versions of Matlab and we don't have matlab to test it.I know people have made it work in the past, but they didn't share how with me (the only example is the one already distributed with irace)

If you get it working, I'll be happy to add it as an example to irace. The more general you make it, the better. Please let us know!

Cheers,

Manuel.

messages.subject: Re: (single) Instance file generation and usage - MATLAB.
parts:
Another possibility is calling Matlab directly from a different programming language and write target-runner in that programming language. For example, write target-runner in Python (there are examples in irace) and call your matlab code:

https://www.mathworks.com/help/matlab/matlab_external/call-matlab-functions-from-python.html

https://www.mathworks.com/help/matlab/matlab_external/call-user-script-and-function-from-python.html

If you know Python, this may be the easiest approach, since handling command-line parameters is very easy in Python and you have examples already of target-runner in Python. Let us know if it works!
